श्री हुँटिराजादिषरूपं नारायणा गणपतिर्नमः ॥३॥ ओ॥ अग्निमीळे पुरोहितं यज्ञस्य देवमृत्विजम् । होतारं रत्नधाततम्॥१॥ अग्निः पूर्वेभिऋषिभिरीड्यो नूतनैरुत स देवाॆ इह वक्षति॥२॥ अग्निना रयिमश्नवत पोषमेव दिवेदिवे। यशसंवीरवत्तमम्॥३॥ अग्ने यं यज्ञमध्वरं विश्वतः परिभूरसि । स इदेवेषु गच्छति॥४॥ अग्निर्होता कवि क्रतुः सत्यश्चित्रश्रवस्तमः । दिवोदेवेभिरागमत्॥५॥ यदङ्गराशुषेत्वमग्नेभदं करिष्यसि। तवेत्तत्सत्यमी गिरः॥६॥ उपत्वाग्ने दिवेदिवो दोषावस्तर्धियावयम्। नमोभरैतमसिराजंतमध्वराणां गोपांऋतस्यदीदिविं वर्धमानमस्वेदमोगसः। पितेवसुनवेचेग्रे सूपा यनोभवस्वावस्यानःस्वस्तये॥७॥ वायवायोयाहिदृशेत मेसोमा अरंकृताः। तेषापा हि श्रुधीहवा॥वाय्

ensemble_tesseract.text: कलाप्य्किशंकं तथा॥९॥ कुमराश्चषयानश्व तथा नक्षत्तारवारिजः॥ ततो नक्षत्रस्तै स्थिताश्च तथैव वारिजे तथा॥१०॥ नक्षत्रातावदारिखे जडमे तरेत्वाक्रमात्॥ षड्-चंद्रशंकनानां च क्रमो यं परिकीर्तितः॥११॥ मध्यरेखापरिज्ञानमाह॥१३॥ द्वै वेदग्नमधोद्विज त्रयस्पार्धै धनं ध्यानं विषतिरगेन चांध्रकिशं॥ वेदैकरायतितथोर्ध्दीगा वरे खातस्याधोगगनमध्ये पुनस्तथैव ॥१२॥ प्रैर्लै चकब्दारवी जंबु स्टांक बुद्दर्वारिजं॥ तद्देयगदितं स्पष्टं शकज्जरमजेषु च ॥१३॥ रेवाणां ना यति च त्रुटयः क्रमेण प्रचितं द्ययनध्र रे जैमान संज्ञं॥ व्यस्तांत ह्यादि तरी खाये चातोग्द्द् श्न्ने ध्दृं जकमथो ततश्रशून्यं ॥१४॥ फरहस्यिपरि री तगानकी स्या द्घादि रे रेखचतुमध्वगेप्पद्धी॥ गगने वक्र तासिधंतदास्याद्विपरीतेजतामा रये लागी ज्या ॥१५॥ अथ धोरेव्याहर्द्ध तदुपरिनन्नो उपरिगतोषुज जो लो ना ये हुर्रमसवरे श्चापि कुमरा ॥ नाये ह्यस्ता सास्पा छज्ञ विधि विंशे शंभुन ने शया ज्ञा रखो ज्ञे यो विमलतर म जे शाक जगते ॥१६॥ शून्यवादयस्पार्घादि योर्द्ध स्वारिष्टि तंततस्तुरै खाश्थ यके क्रमेण॥ तथा च शून्य त्रयमह्र शंखि तं रे रेख दास्या त्तदध्वश्रतियगा॥१७॥ नक्षत्रतारवारिज संज्ञ के नाये चादंतव रवारिजसं ज्ञ कं ते तथा न्यतः॥ व्यस्तांत भवति यदा रिवला निधं स द्विजेयंस काभमिदं

gemini.text:
Verse 23: On the seventh day, Sunday, at the time of the rising of the lunar mansion (nakshatra) Ketu, amidst a pure and elevated setting, 23.

In the central line of the gem-necklace born from the plowshare, within the belly [of the setting], resides a radiant gem endowed with judgment and precious qualities, along with removing troubles, 23.

Upon the half-moon, as well as [auspicious] signs and filaments upon all limbs, 23.

Three divine luminous realms they hold, golden, pure, and purified by duty; unblinking, unassailed, they sit, widely praised, swift for the mortal. You are the kings, wide-ruling over all, gods like fierce demons (asuras) in thought. Do not let Mitra, the protector against demons, pass us by; measure out our lifespans, preserve those of the ancients. You know the rivers, O Ādityas, flowing east and west, and the deep sight. Truly, he goes first with his chariot, wealthy and worthy of worship from dawn. Pure, resting upon his own pasture, he dwells well-nourished, heroic. No one, O Brahma, is far or near from the guidance of the Ādityas.

gemini.text: It brings about our deep meditative absorption (samadhi), attenuates the afflictions, and renders ineffective the seeds of those afflictions that have been burnt by the fire of discriminative discernment (prasamkhyana), making them incapable of producing further effects. In order to further attenuate those [afflictions], the realization of the distinction between the true Self and the [primordial] matter—which is untouched by the afflictions, actions, results, or latent impressions—culminates in subtle discernment. Having fulfilled their purpose, [the gunas] cause those [afflictions] to resolve back into their source (pratiprasava). Through the attenuation of these [afflictions], [one might ask]: how are they further subdued? [The answer is given in the sutra:] "Avidya (ignorance) is the field for the subsequent ones—whether dormant, attenuated, intercepted, or fully active" (Yoga Sutras II.4). Here, avidya is the breeding ground for the subsequent ones, namely asmita (egoism) and the others, which exist in four states: dormant, attenuated, intercepted, or fully active. Among these, the dormant state is when the mental modifications are merely latent in the mind-stuff like a seed; the attenuated state is when they manifest only when stimulated by their objects.

When the text states, "Now, the instruction on Yoga is to be understood as the authorized treatise," this establishes the authority of the science of Yoga. One might object: Is Yoga authorized through inferential reasoning, or through the Manusmriti? To this, the text replies that it is to be known. Having heard this directly through the traditional method of study, it is stated that Yoga [is established] through that very authoritative treatise, and not merely by some other means. 

Because the activity pertains to the agent and not merely to outward ritual action, and because the subject matter of Yoga falls within the domain of this authoritative treatise, the underlying intent is that Yoga itself is indeed what is authorized as the proper sphere of the scripture's operation. 

Furthermore, regarding the twofold nature of this authority, the exegetical text composed by the master Galāḷayi—which serves to remove doubts—endures perpetually. Where there is no doubt regarding the words themselves, no doubt regarding the meaning can arise. 

"Yoga" means *samādhi* (absorption or deep meditation), derived from the verbal root *yuj*, meaning *samādhau* (to concentrate or absorb), according to the authority of the sacred texts (Śruti), and not from the root *yujir* in the sense of mere connection (*samyoga*), which bears the meaning of conjunction. 

One might raise the question: Is the instruction on Yoga to be understood as an authorized scripture? Yes. Yoga is *samādhi*. And *samādhi* is not liberation (*mokṣa*); rather, it is a quality or state of the mind (*cittasya dharma*).

Neither grass nor the like is the subject of explanation at this time; rather, the preparation of medicine is for purification and pacification. Thus, in brief, medicine is twofold, and knowledge of the body is the supreme and ultimate means to counteract diseases in proper order. Just as emesis and purgation are used in vomiting, similarly, oil mixed with honey, drunk along with [the appropriate substance], serves as an excellent remedy for mental disorders. 

The physician, having known this, [attends to] the feet of the patient; the treatments are established in the heart. What are the specific qualities there? Then, one should quickly satisfy the thirst of the afflicted with water. The physician, having summoned the fivefold procedure, [performs] the incantation for the dispelling of diseases. Here, the intelligent person, knowing the blood well, [acts] with obstructionists. 

By the command of the physician in the chamber of the patient, epilepsy and skin diseases are treated with the best of all medicines. The pacification of exertion for a man of controlled self [is achieved] here; the affliction having been diminished, the destruction of the obstacle to knowledge is attained. 

In that household where one resorts to the protection [of the physician], where the path of righteousness flows like nectar, and where the means such as surgical instruments [are available], the disease arising from an angered state is completely subdued. By the practice of wholesome regimen, freedom from illness is attained, and here is the ripening of merit.

Salutation to Lord Dundhiraja! Salutation to Lord Ganapati! Om!

I praise Agni, the domestic priest of the sacrifice, the divine minister, the hotar, the best bestower of wealth.

Agni, who is to be praised by ancient sages and by modern ones as well, may He bring the gods hither.

Through Agni, one obtains wealth, daily nourishment, and fame accompanied by heroic offspring.

O Agni, whatever sacrificial ritual you encompass on all sides, that indeed reaches the gods.

Agni is the hotar, possessing the wisdom of a sage, truthful, possessing most wondrous renown; may the god come with the gods.

Whatever blessing, O Agni, you will bestow upon the pious worshipper, that truth belongs to you alone, O Angiras.

Unto you, O Agni, day by day, O guardian of the night, we bring our prayers, paying homage—to you who rule over the dark, the protector of sacrifices, the shining guardian of cosmic order, growing in your own abode.

O Agni, be easily accessible to us like a father to his son; abide with us for our well-being.

O Vayu, come hither, O handsome one; these Soma-juices have been prepared. Drink of them and listen to our call.

Worshippers ask Agni for daily nourishment, fame, blessings, and fatherly protection, while also inviting the handsome god Vayu to drink the prepared Soma-juice and listen to their call.

Salutation to Sri. Salutation to Sri Ganesha. Salutation to Sri Purushottama. Salutation to Sri Kirtanadri. May He who, through the forest-like path of worldly existence, binds and cures the ailments of the universe along with Uma and others, the dispeller of darkness, the supreme physician for the afflictions beginning with passion and other diseases—to that Supreme Light, I offer my prostrations.

Now we shall expound upon this treatise, fulfilling the foremost desires [of the seekers]. As stated: "For one desiring longevity, righteousness, wealth, and the means to all accomplishments, utmost regard should be bestowed upon the science of life (Ayurveda) in every way." 

Brahma remembered the Veda of longevity and imparted it to Prajapati. Prajapati taught the Ashvini twins, and they instructed Dhanvantari. Dhanvantari taught Bharadvaja and others, and they composed various treatises. For the benefit of those whose intellects are feeble, this essence is gathered here, avoiding unnecessary prolixity.

The eight branches of this [science] are: internal medicine (Kayachikitsa), pediatrics (Balachikitsa), psychiatry (Graharoga), treatment of diseases of the upper body/ENT (Urdhvanga), surgery (Shalyatantra), toxicology (Danshtratantra/Agadatantra), geriatrics (Jaratantra/Rasayana), and aphrodisiacs (Vajikaranatantra). 

In brief, the three humors (doshas) are Vata, Pitta, and Kapha.

It then introduces a treatise on Ayurveda, stating that the science of life should be studied for longevity, righteousness, wealth, and accomplishments, tracing its lineage from Brahma down to various sages. Finally, it outlines the eight branches of this medical science and lists the three bodily humors as Vata, Pitta, and Kapha.

Heavy, soft, oily, unctuous, stable, and firm properties constitute the physical qualities, whereas their alterations lead to various disorders. Diseases arise from the improper or excessive combination of time, intellect, and action (Karma). 

Through the threefold measure of proper application, under-application, or excessive application, illness or health ensues. Doubt regarding disease, its severity, balance, or complete eradication (health) is understood through the systematic division of endogenous and exogenous disorders, which are broadly classified into two categories. Their locus of manifestation is also twofold, classified by body and mind. Rajas and Tamas represent the mental coverings associated with diseases. 

A physician should examine patients through observation (darshana), palpation/touch (sparsha), and interrogation (प्रश्न/prashna). The diagnosis of a disease is established by understanding its etiology (nidana), prodromal symptoms (praag-upakshana), actual symptoms, and therapeutic tests (upashaya). By means of careful differentiation, mixed symptoms, and clear intellect, a wise physician eradicates disease at its root. Thus, based on the three fundamental humors (doshas)—vata, pitta, and kapha—in their balanced, aggravated, or diminished states, the manifestations of bodily conditions are ascertained.
pipeline_records.explanation: Kapha and Pitta symptoms are pacified by specific treatments and substances, while the potency of substances is twofold (hot and cold) and their post-digestive effect is threefold (sweet, sour, and pungent). Diseases are caused by the improper or excessive combination of time, intellect, and action, resulting in either illness or health based on proper, under, or excessive application. A physician examines patients through observation, touch, and questioning to diagnose and eradicate diseases by understanding their causes, symptoms, and bodily humors.

Salutation to Lord Ganesha. Salutation to the sweet form. 

May the lotus feet of Ganesha, which the bees of his flowing temporal ichor eagerly touch, and which bestow mental peace and liberation from great impurities, dispel our worldly afflictions and grant auspicious intellect. (1)

That supreme, multifaceted entity, pervading the quarters, radiant like the moon, subtle and profound, which is sought by the wise—I shall now expound according to the tradition. (2)

I shall set forth the captivating and diverse aspects of the science of the human body (Tajika/astrological or bodily science), as declared of old by Rama, the knower of the gods, and by the Yavanas. (3)

[One should know the system] offering auspicious flowers to the deity Ganesha, removing all obstacles and defects, and fulfilling the desires of the devotees. (4)

[Regarding the bodily marks or lines]: By the standard of apertures, one should understand the Hindu system of measurements. Following the left-hand path in proper sequence, one should determine the stable positions. (5)

From the presence of lines, one result arises; in the absence of lines (zero), another result arises accordingly. Through the application of the rule of lines and zeros, the zero itself is understood. Counting through the four places in order, cutting the fifth, the sixth is declared as measured above. (6)

Whatever result arises in the ninth and tenth places through the combination of yoga, and in the sequence of the expenditure of knowledge, that difference between the eighth and ninth should be known as productive of a king. (7)

In the Vipra, the Daiva, the Samjna, the Shakula, four are declared. When there is a yoga of these two, then it produces a king free from destruction. (8)

Thus is the sequence of the first results. First is the Kusupya, then the Kudarivila, then the Kuduravarija, followed by Umataparahoha, and so forth.

सेत्रमुतरेषांप्रसुवृत्तनुविच्छिनोदाराणां ४ अत्रअविद्यासे

pipeline_records.translation:
It brings about deep meditative absorption (samadhi) and weakens the mental afflictions (kleshas). Having thus weakened the kleshas, it burns their seed-nature with the fire of discriminative discernment (prasamkhyana), rendering them incapable of sprouting again. Through this attenuation, the kleshas—no longer touching the self like unbaked clay—culminate in a subtle state of direct insight, which is the sole realization of the distinction between the pure consciousness and the mind. Once their function is fulfilled, they merge back into their primal source (pratiprasava). 

Regarding this, one might ask: what and how numerous are these kleshas? Here, the answer is given: the field and birthplace for ignorance (avidya) and the subsequent [afflictions—asmita, raga, dvesha, and abhinivesha]—which manifest in four states: dormant (prasupta), attenuated (tanu), intercepted (vicchinna), and fully active (udara). 

Among these, the dormancy of desire consists of the mind remaining anchored merely in the potentiality of attachment without active expression. Its awakening is its direct manifestation when stimulated by its object.
pipeline_records.explanation: This text explains that meditation weakens mental afflictions and burns their seeds through discriminative discernment so they cannot grow back. These afflictions exist in four states—dormant, attenuated, intercepted, and fully active—with ignorance serving as their birthplace and field. Furthermore, desire remains dormant when the mind holds only the potential for attachment, and it awakens when stimulated by an object.

pipeline_records.translation:
Om. Salutations to Lord Ganesha. Now begins the second pada. 

How does the yoga of a person whose mind is unified relate to one whose mind is distracted? To explain this, Kriya Yoga is introduced: austerities (tapas), recitation of sacred texts (svadhyaya), and devotion to the Lord (ishvara-pranidhana) constitute Kriya Yoga. 

Yoga does not succeed for one who merely practices austerities without these. The mind, deeply stained by beginningless karma-vasanas and entangled in the net of sensory objects, cannot be pierced without the union of austerities. Therefore, austerities are to be undertaken because they produce a state of mental clarity without causing harm; thus it is considered worthy of practice. 

Svadhyaya is the repetition of sacred mantras such as Om, or the study of scriptures on liberation. Ishvara-pranidhana is the offering of all actions to the Supreme Guru and the renunciation of their fruits. 

This Kriya Yoga is to be practiced for the purpose of cultivating samadhi and for attenuating the afflictions (kleshas).
pipeline_records.explanation: In simple terms, this statement expresses that om.

pipeline_records.translation:
When the word "adas" (that) implies an unchanging reality and true expression, one asks: "What is this pertaining to the domain of the authoritative treatises?" It is replied: "It should be known that the discipline of yoga is that which is to be understood through authoritative scriptural reasoning." Having heard this from the teacher of death, since that is not connected with mere worldly reasoning, and since water's activity does not pertain to the realm of action, it should be understood that the scriptural authority pertains to the subject of yoga due to the intention of expressing the agent's activity. Since the scriptural activity pertains to the realm of yoga, yoga alone is authorized—such is the underlying intent. 

Moreover, this word indicates the meaning of authority; hence, by removing the doubt regarding the syllable... raises the doubt: What is yoga? Yoga is *samādhi* (meditation/absorption). Derived from the root *yuj* in the sense of *samādhi*, [it is defined as] one who has mastered *samādhi* through it, not merely in the sense of *saṃyoga* (union/junction)—such is the meaning. 

Now, one should understand that the treatise is authorized for the teaching of yoga. Yoga is *samādhi*. And that [samādhi] is common to all levels of the ground [of the mind]; it is a quality of the mind.
pipeline_records.explanation: The passage explains that authoritative scripture applies to the domain of yoga, which is defined as *samādhi* (meditation or absorption) rather than mere worldly reasoning or physical action. It clarifies that the root word refers specifically to mastery in *samādhi* rather than simple union. Finally, it states that this *samādhi* is common to all levels of the mind and is a quality of the mind itself.
pipeline_records.keywords: Yoga, Samādhi, Scriptural authority, Śāstra, Citta-dharma, Adhikāra

pipeline_records.translation: By those means also one should accomplish the stability of the mind. Or else, a sensory-oriented activity (vishayavati pravrittir) arising in the mind binds it to stability. When one concentrates upon the tip of the nose, there arises the experience and perception of divine fragrance; at the tip of the tongue, the experience of divine taste; at the palate, the perception of form; in the middle of the tongue, the experience of divine touch; and at the root of the tongue, the perception of divine sound. These generated activities bind the mind to stability, dispel doubt, and become the gateways to meditative wisdom (samadhi-prajna). By this same principle, it is to be understood that activities arising in regard to the moon, sun, planets, jewels, lamps, and rays of light are likewise sensory-oriented (vishayavati). Even though the truth—as comprehended through scripture, inference, and the instruction of a preceptor—becomes fully illuminated by wisdom, possessing the capacity to establish reality accurately, yet so long as even a single aspect is not directly perceived by one's own internal instruments (antahkarana), all of it remains as if indirect (paroksha) and fails to generate a firm conviction regarding subtle matters such as liberation and the like. Therefore, for the purpose of subduing [doubt and indirectness] alongside scripture, inference, and the preceptor's instruction...
pipeline_records.explanation: The mind's stability can be achieved by focusing on sensory activities, such as concentrating on the tip of the nose to experience divine fragrance, or on different parts of the tongue and palate to perceive divine taste, form, touch, and sound. These experiences stabilize the mind, remove doubt, and lead to meditative wisdom, similar to focusing on the sun, moon, jewels, or lights. However, even when truth is taught by scriptures, logic, and teachers, it remains somewhat indirect until at least one aspect is directly experienced by one's own internal senses to firmly establish conviction in subtle matters like liberation.

pipeline_records.translation: O Lord, within your body I see all the gods, as well as the diverse hosts of beings—Lord Brahma seated upon the lotus, all the seers, and the divine serpents.
pipeline_records.explanation: The speaker looks inside the body of the Lord and sees all the gods, different groups of living beings, and Lord Brahma sitting on a lotus. Also visible inside the body are all the seers and the divine serpents.
pipeline_records.keywords: Visvarupa, cosmic vision, divine form, Brahma, seers, serpents

pipeline_records.ocr_text:
॥श्रीरामाय नमः॥ उं०का
रंषंममेमलं निरा
कारव्यापतते सच
रातस्मईश्रीगुरवेन
म परमगुरवेनम॥
pipeline_records.translation: Salutation to Sri Rama! Salutation to that holy Guru, who is of the nature of the syllable Om, faultless, formless, all-pervading, and present in all moving and unmoving beings; salutation also to the Supreme Guru.
pipeline_records.explanation: This passage begins with a greeting to Sri Rama. It then offers salutations to the holy Guru, describing him as formless, faultless, all-pervading, existing in all moving and unmoving beings, and having the nature of the syllable Om. Finally, it offers a salutation to the Supreme Guru.
pipeline_records.keywords: Sri Rama, Guru Vandana, Omkara, Nirakara, Paramaguru, Mangalacharan

pipeline_records.ocr_text:
तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा ।
अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा ॥ १३ ॥
pipeline_records.translation: There, at that time, the son of Pandu beheld the entire universe, divided in many ways, yet standing as one in the body of the god of gods.
pipeline_records.explanation: At that time, Arjuna, the son of Pandu, looked upon the body of the supreme god. Within that divine body, he saw the entire universe existing together as one, even though it was divided in many different ways.
pipeline_records.keywords: Vishvarupa, Cosmic Form, Bhagavad Gita, Divine Vision, Arjuna, Universe
